target_outcome: research-grade release candidate with explicit external gates

findings.evidence: A two-activity counterexample showed the former Hall cut rejected an exactly room-feasible alternative when room eligibility changed with start time.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: All decomposed solves with time-varying room availability, closures, locks, or interval domains.
findings.root_cause: A fixed-incumbent Hall witness was generalized to every start covering the witness slot without proving the alternative candidate domain stayed within the witnessed room set.
findings.proposed_change: Generate a contextual Hall inequality only for starts whose exact cluster-aware candidate domain is a subset of the witness rooms; otherwise emit the exact incumbent nogood.
findings.regression_risk: Incorrect domain reconstruction could still remove a feasible master pattern.
findings.required_tests: Counterexample regression plus exhaustive tiny-domain enumeration against the exact room subproblem.
findings.before_measurement: Known exactly room-feasible alternative was declared INFEASIBLE after the cut.
findings.after_measurement: Alternative remains feasible; exhaustive 4x4 availability-domain enumeration found no feasible pattern removed; contextual and fallback paths both exercised.
findings.independent_review_result: Solver-audit subagent reproduced the defect, implemented the correction, and ran 32 neighboring tests successfully.

findings.evidence: Local search accepted activity-specific forbidden starts that the strict validator rejected.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Local improvement and live-progress candidate generation under imported or institution-specific time domains.
findings.root_cause: The incremental placement predicate omitted activity forbidden starts and institutional start-window checks.
findings.proposed_change: Share the canonical time-domain rules in the placement predicate and revalidate every candidate before incumbent replacement.
findings.regression_risk: Over-restricting moves if institutional window semantics diverge from solver domains.
findings.required_tests: Forbidden-start and institutional-window regressions plus strict-validator parity.
findings.before_measurement: Minimal forbidden move returned allowed while strict validation emitted an error.
findings.after_measurement: Ten local-search validation tests pass and service-level incumbent validation remains enforced.
findings.independent_review_result: Reproduced and reviewed by solver-audit subagent.

findings.evidence: Incremental move deltas omitted soft distribution penalties; a controlled SameDays move missed exactly 1000 objective units.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Every local-search run with positive soft distribution constraints.
findings.root_cause: The delta cache covered group, staff, stability, and room terms but not typed distribution constraints.
findings.proposed_change: Index positive constraints by activity and evaluate only the deduplicated affected subset before and after a move.
findings.regression_risk: Hot-path overhead and double-counting constraints shared by multiple moved activities.
findings.required_tests: Exact full-score versus incremental-delta parity and a no-distribution hot-path test.
findings.after_measurement: Exact parity regression passes; the no-positive-constraint path skips collection entirely.
findings.independent_review_result: Implemented and benchmark-path reviewed by solver-audit subagent.

findings.evidence: Greedy rooming rejected ITC-2007 schedules for room overflow even though imported capacity is a soft constraint.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Greedy ITC-2007 baselines and any institutional profile with soft room capacity.
findings.root_cause: Greedy eligibility applied capacity unconditionally instead of honoring the canonical hard flag.
findings.proposed_change: Condition capacity filtering on the hard flag and use overflow as an assignment cost when soft.
findings.regression_risk: Hard-capacity instances could accidentally admit overflow.
findings.required_tests: Greedy/decomposed parity under soft capacity and retained hard-capacity rejection.
findings.before_measurement: A one-course ITC instance failed greedy extraction with capacity reason.
findings.after_measurement: Greedy admits overflow, selects the lower-overflow room, and matches the exact room subproblem in focused tests.
findings.independent_review_result: Reproduced and fixed by solver-audit subagent.

findings.evidence: The fairness-first path now builds and strictly validates a feasibility incumbent before bounded fairness optimization, and preserves that incumbent when the fairness stage returns UNKNOWN.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Bounded fairness-first and objective decomposed solves.
findings.root_cause: The remaining wall budget was handed wholesale to the first objective master solve.
findings.proposed_change: Reserve room-validation time, separate feasibility incumbent construction from bounded improvement, and report build/master/room time explicitly.
findings.regression_risk: Too much reservation may reduce objective quality on easy room instances.
findings.required_tests: Small finite-budget incumbent test, strict deadline tolerance, and objective-quality comparison.
findings.before_measurement: small_demo at 5 seconds used about 5.01 seconds in the master then returned TIME_LIMIT/UNKNOWN.
findings.after_measurement: fairness_first small_demo seed 1 returned a complete 182/182-activity, strict-room-valid incumbent in 4.9188 seconds under a 5-second budget and in 7.7958 seconds under an 8-second budget, with no deadline overrun. When fairness remained UNKNOWN, the result was explicitly FEASIBLE with status FEASIBILITY_INCUMBENT_FAIRNESS_INCOMPLETE rather than OPTIMAL.
findings.independent_review_result: Solver-audit verification passed 40 affected adaptive/decomposition/profile tests and 140 broad solver/research/ITC/proof-lineage tests; API/product/workflow serialization added 23 passes with one expected socket skip.
findings.final_disposition: Keep. Fairness optimality remains explicitly incomplete when the second phase times out; two full release verification passes are still required.

findings.evidence: The ITC-2007 converter originally post-scored four official terms but the solver objective did not optimize minimum working days or curriculum compactness.
findings.root_cause: Benchmark semantics were not compiled into the CP objective.
findings.proposed_change: Compile all four official weighted terms for integrated room CP and reject unsupported objective configurations explicitly.
findings.regression_risk: A modeling mismatch between CP objective and independent scorer.
findings.required_tests: CP objective equals independent scorer and official validator component agreement.
findings.before_measurement: Benchmark score represented unguided feasibility rather than a fair optimization comparison.
findings.after_measurement: Sixteen objective/interchange tests pass; comp01 produced identical internal total 1602 and official validator total 1602 with zero hard violations.
findings.independent_review_result: Competitor-benchmark subagent identified the defect; independent official C++ validator agreed on the pilot.

findings.evidence: A common 10-second, one-worker, seed-17 pilot on ITC-2007 comp01-comp05 produced official-validator-feasible outputs for both Planora and CPSolver/UniTime; the competitor had the lower official objective on all five instances.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Research claims of competitive or superior optimization performance.
findings.root_cause: The exact CP objective lacks a strong benchmark-specific incumbent and the prior research acceptance scorer was not guaranteed to use the official objective.
findings.proposed_change: Use official-objective acceptance, fast validated hints, and a common identical-condition harness before selecting further optimization work.
findings.regression_risk: Benchmark-specific tuning could reduce generality or create unfair time accounting.
findings.required_tests: Official-validator checked paired runs across the complete corpus with identical budgets, seeds, CPU limits, and disclosed build time.
findings.before_measurement: Planora 1602 at 10 seconds; UniTime 6 at 1 second on comp01 seed 11 under non-equivalent conditions.
findings.after_measurement: Under the controlled pilot, Planora scored 554, 763, 777, 1411, and 1333 versus CPSolver/UniTime 5, 176, 163, 67, and 612 on comp01-comp05 respectively. Both solvers had zero official hard violations.
findings.independent_review_result: The competitor-benchmark track implemented the common harness, official-validator bridge, source-file hashing, official objective parity, and benchmark-metadata-gated course-orbit symmetry breaking. The uncontended symmetry-off/on matrix and full controlled corpus matrix remain pending.
findings.final_disposition: Open; current pilot disfavors Planora and no competitive or superiority claim is permitted until the official controlled matrix is complete.

findings.evidence: ITC-2019 requires alternate configurations, class hierarchies, time/room domains, distribution constraints, and student sectioning; prior inspection-only support could not substantiate compatibility.
findings.root_cause: The earlier component counted XML structures but did not preserve or solve their semantics.
findings.proposed_change: Add lossless semantic parsing, conditional CP-SAT sectioning, independent local validators, and official solution XML interchange.
findings.regression_risk: Untested official distribution types or corpus edge cases.
findings.required_tests: Official corpus parse, official distribution/objective validator agreement, and known-score fixtures.
findings.after_measurement: Representative synthetic alternate-configuration, hierarchy, capacity, travel, validation, and XML round-trip tests pass.
findings.independent_review_result: Implemented by the ITC-2019 subagent; official corpus was unavailable locally and public early instances require an account.
findings.final_disposition: Keep local implementation; external claim remains blocked by corpus and official validator access.

findings.evidence: Historical experiment rows reused identical generated instances under different seed labels and mixed retries/fallbacks into algorithm runtimes.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Every statistical and performance claim in the paper.
findings.root_cause: Seeds were not passed into named generators and run identity did not isolate primary attempts.
findings.proposed_change: Hash normalized instances, isolate primary attempts, require zero validator errors/no fallback, and gate every condition on 30 unique effective hashes.
findings.regression_risk: Publication gate could be bypassed by old rows or duplicated hashes.
findings.required_tests: Duplicate-seed/hash rejection, invalid/fallback exclusion, and nonzero gate exit.
findings.before_measurement: Historical 24/24 reliability and speed claims were not inferentially valid.
findings.after_measurement: Seven experiment-statistics/reproducibility tests pass. The 30-instance-per-condition feasibility matrix has not completed publication-gate analysis, so no condition has been promoted to publication evidence.
findings.independent_review_result: Gate logic reviewed in separate competitor and solver tracks.
findings.final_disposition: Historical results quarantined; execute the 30-instance matrix before paper claims.

findings.evidence: Broad novelty claims conflict with established work on Hall decomposition, Benders timetabling, CP-repair LNS, adaptive neighborhoods, and bandit-selected LNS.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Paper novelty, presentation credibility, and peer review.
findings.root_cause: The initial contribution framing combined individually established methods without a systematic boundary review.
findings.proposed_change: Withdraw mathematical and broad algorithmic novelty claims; evaluate only the integrated, auditable systems construction and preregister falsifying ablations.
findings.regression_risk: Unindexed prior work may still anticipate the narrowed construction.
findings.required_tests: Independent second-reviewer database search, proof-lineage replay and tamper tests, and cut/neighborhood ablations on 30 effective instances per condition.
findings.after_measurement: The adversarial review falsified the contextual Hall inequality as a new family and falsified broad Benders/certificate-guided and explanation/core-guided LNS novelty. Locally, SHA-256 content-addressed certificate, cut, derivation, and room-context IDs; complete Hall evidence; an independent replay checker; exact-nogood fallback for rejected evidence; and lineage propagation into adaptive-LNS traces are implemented and focused tests reject altered or incomplete evidence.
findings.independent_review_result: A separate proof-lineage implementation track passed 24 focused tests and broader solver/research verification. Literature screening remains single-reviewer and requires an independent external reviewer before submission.
findings.final_disposition: Do not claim a novel inequality or broadly novel search method. Treat the integrated auditable systems pipeline as an unestablished empirical hypothesis until ablations and independent literature review pass.

findings.evidence: Constraint and solver configuration previously required technical knowledge and exposed low-level choices without an administrator decision flow.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Administrators and nontechnical scheduling staff creating a new scenario.
findings.root_cause: Settings were organized around solver parameters rather than institutional outcomes and evidence boundaries.
findings.proposed_change: Add a five-step administrator wizard for scenario, institution, priorities, uncertainty, and review; apply policies server-side and recommend a solver profile.
findings.regression_risk: A friendly preset could be mistaken for an institutionally validated policy.
findings.required_tests: Typecheck, lint, production build, API contract tests, keyboard/accessibility checks, and screenshot-based responsive review.
findings.after_measurement: TypeScript, ESLint, Vite build, 30 focused UI/API tests, and one live loopback API test pass.
findings.independent_review_result: Screenshot/browser audit awaits explicit Playwright permission under the product-design workflow.
findings.final_disposition: Functional implementation retained; visual/browser gate remains open.

findings.evidence: The SS23 import represented 15 observed nonblank room labels plus 146 row-scoped UNSPECIFIED placeholders as 161 modeled rooms.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: GIU scale, room-capacity, and institutional-calibration claims.
findings.root_cause: Synthetic placeholder resources were conflated with confirmed physical rooms.
findings.proposed_change: Separate observed labels from placeholders, attach source hashes and inference status, and remove unsupported policy defaults.
findings.regression_risk: Reducing the synthetic room pool may invalidate historical scale smokes or make the preset infeasible.
findings.required_tests: Reproducible calibration extraction, source-hash check, preset assertions, and updated scale benchmark wording.
findings.before_measurement: 161 rooms could be misread as an institutional fact.
findings.after_measurement: A hash-locked calibration artifact now distinguishes 15 historically observed nonblank room labels from 146 row-scoped UNSPECIFIED placeholders, uses nominal demand, retains only the five historically observed starts, and disables unsupported calendar/building/travel policies. The current import projection has 148 validation errors: 93 synthetic staff overlaps, 39 inferred room-type or specialization mismatches, and 16 room overlaps.
findings.independent_review_result: Local calibration extraction, source-hash checks, preset assertions, and the institutional validation protocol are implemented. No institutional stakeholder has supplied current ground truth or signed the preset and artifact hashes.
findings.final_disposition: Keep as a historical research preset only. Current GIU policy calibration, validator agreement, and institutional sign-off remain OPEN.

findings.evidence: The checkout pinned PyJWT 2.10.1, which was covered by current security advisories, and production mode accepted any nonempty authentication secret regardless of byte length.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: JWT-backed production sessions and deployments with weak PLANORA_AUTH_SECRET configuration.
findings.root_cause: The dependency pin predated the advisory fixes, and startup validation checked secret presence but not a minimum cryptographic key length.
findings.proposed_change: Pin PyJWT[crypto] 2.13.0 and reject production authentication secrets shorter than 32 UTF-8 bytes; document generation of a 48-byte random secret.
findings.regression_risk: Existing deployments with short secrets will fail closed at startup and require an intentional secret rotation.
findings.required_tests: Dependency-version check, short-production-secret rejection, JWT algorithm/issuer/audience tests, and the focused security/operations suite.
findings.before_measurement: PyJWT 2.10.1 was installed and a one-byte nonempty production secret passed configuration loading.
findings.after_measurement: The local environment reports PyJWT 2.13.0; production rejects secrets shorter than 32 UTF-8 bytes; 43 security/operations tests passed with one deselected slow case, and a focused 26-test auth/security pass plus Ruff completed successfully during the fix.
findings.independent_review_result: Local secret-pattern scanning found no repository matches and offline npm production and full audits reported zero vulnerabilities. The Python advisory audit did not complete and the formal Codex Security desktop scan is separately blocked, so these checks are not a full security clearance.
findings.final_disposition: Keep; rotate any short deployment secret before startup. Do not call the repository security-cleared until the open advisory and formal-scan gates are resolved.

findings.evidence: The required Codex Security desktop scan lifecycle tools are not exposed in the active tool inventory, so a formal repository scan could not be started, monitored, or completed.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Release security sign-off and any claim that the formal Codex Security workflow completed.
findings.root_cause: The active desktop environment lacks the required scan lifecycle capability; local tests and pattern searches are not an equivalent formal scan.
findings.proposed_change: Expose the Codex Security desktop lifecycle tools and run the configured repository scan, or obtain explicit release-owner approval for a documented equivalent review.
findings.regression_risk: Treating local fallback checks as the formal scan would create false assurance and omit lifecycle-owned findings.
findings.required_tests: Formal scan reaches a terminal state, all findings are triaged, fixes are independently validated, and closure evidence is recorded.
findings.before_measurement: No current formal Codex Security scan result exists for this working tree.
findings.independent_review_result: Blocked before scan dispatch because the required lifecycle tools are unavailable; no scan ownership, scan ID, or clean result is claimed.
findings.final_disposition: OPEN release gate; a formal scan or explicitly approved equivalent remains required.

findings.evidence: Adaptive exact repair rebuilt a complete CP-room objective model every round; locks reduced freedom but not model size.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Research-adaptive quality improvement on medium and large instances.
findings.root_cause: Neighborhoods were implemented as fixed variables on fresh full models.
findings.proposed_change: Reuse one exact model with assumptions and incumbent hints; report build/setup/search separately. A true restricted builder remains future work.
findings.regression_risk: Assumption leakage or stale hints across rounds.
findings.required_tests: Assumption reset/core correctness, validated monotone incumbent, deadline enforcement, and model-build count.
findings.before_measurement: small_demo full objective model: 18,390 variables/38,542 constraints rebuilt per round; mixed_large: 214,282/482,382.
findings.after_measurement: A 260-activity pilot built once in 0.521 seconds and used about 0.022 seconds setup per round; the reusable model still contained 26,572 variables/58,008 constraints.
findings.independent_review_result: Solver-audit review confirms reuse reduces rebuild overhead but not model size.
findings.final_disposition: Keep reuse; do not claim restricted model size.

findings.evidence: The existing release/v1.0 snapshot predates the current solver, benchmark, calibration, wizard, proof-lineage, dependency-security, and research changes. A new checksum-verified research release-candidate bundle now captures the current worktree, compiled paper, coverage/source binding, benchmark evidence, and explicit NO-GO boundary; the controlled benchmark, publication matrix, UI browser audit, external institutional/validator gates, and two-pass verification remain incomplete.
findings.affected_users_or_workflows: Any packaged handoff or release-candidate claim.
findings.root_cause: Release artifacts were frozen before the active hardening loop completed.
findings.proposed_change: Regenerate only after all required evidence gates, then verify checksums and run two consecutive full release passes.
findings.regression_risk: Freezing a dirty or incompletely verified tree can package stale or untracked files.
findings.required_tests: Artifact checksum verifier, offline smoke, full test/lint/type/build/paper checks twice.
findings.after_measurement: The immutable v1.0-rc-20260813-research-ready bundle was generated and independently verified against its required contents, nested evidence, coverage-source manifest, paper freshness, and SHA-256 manifest. The bundle truthfully records a dirty worktree and a NO-GO external-readiness gate.
findings.independent_review_result: The consolidated non-slow, slow, coverage-ratchet, release-contract, paper, and tamper-resistance checks passed. The exact immutable bundle was then independently verified a second time. These checks close artifact regeneration and integrity, but they are not a substitute for the required consecutive full release passes or external agreements.
findings.final_disposition: Keep the verified research release-candidate bundle as an auditable internal handoff. NO-GO remains for external-readiness, publication-superiority, institutional-readiness, security-clearance, and full product-acceptance claims until their separate gates pass.
